About This Log

ℹ This transmission originates from deep space. Signal latency: 4.2 years.

Stellar Log is a personal transmission journal of Mr. Collin Mizner, astrophysicist and sole crew member aboard the Interstellar Science Vessel Perihelion.

The Mission

Launched in 2380 under the auspices of the Terran Exploration Consortium, Perihelion's seven-year mission is to conduct close-range survey operations of systems within the 5 light-year radius beyond the Heliopause — the boundary where the Sun's solar wind yields to interstellar space.

Collin's role: observe, measure, document, and transmit. Everything she discovers, Earth won't know about for over four years.

The Explorer

Mr. Mizner holds degrees in astrophysics and astrobiology from the University of São Paulo and the Orbital Institute of Sciences. She was selected from over 12,000 applicants for the program, citing her ability to "tolerate extended isolation with grace." She would tell you that's debatable.

Before departure he spent three years in analog mission training in the Arctic and at the Martian South Pole base. Neither prepared her for the specific quality of silence at 4 light-years from home.

The Ship

Perihelion is a 340-meter autonomous research vessel with an AI flight management system called CASS (Crew Autonomy Support System). CASS doesn't talk — it chirps status codes and adjusts cabin temperature without being asked. Collin has mixed feelings about this.

Why Public Logs?

The Consortium requires all mission personnel to maintain public transmission logs. The stated reason is scientific transparency. Mira suspects it's also to remind him that someone, eventually, will read these.

Transmissions are relayed via the deep-space network at 14-day intervals. Earth receipt is delayed by approximately 4.2 years.

Explorer vessel Perihelion — Navigator: Dr. Mira Vasquez — Mission Year 7

Current Position: 12h 39m 42s RA • +11° 24' Dec
